$$

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic sine function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}.
$$

 

And the product rule is

$$
\frac{\text{d}(u\cdot v)}{\text{d}x}={u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)+u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)
$$

Using the product rule, chain rule, and  formula above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(x) & ={({e}^{x})}^{′}\cdot \operatorname{arsinh}⁡(4x+3)+{e}^{x}\cdot {(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡(4x+3))}^{′} \\  & ={e}^{x}\cdot \operatorname{arsinh}⁡(4x+3)+{e}^{x}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{(4x+3)^{2}+1}}\cdot {(4x+3)}^{′} \\  & ={e}^{x}\cdot \operatorname{arsinh}⁡(4x+3)+{e}^{x}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{(4x+3)^{2}+1}}\cdot 4 \\  & ={e}^{x}\,\operatorname{arsinh}⁡(4x+3)+\frac{4{e}^{x}}{\sqrt{(4x+3)^{2}+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$
